$comment: Drop MP3s (or anything <audio> decodes) into public/audio/clickwheel/tracks/
and add a row here.
FILENAMES ARE lowercase ASCII, digits and hyphens. No spaces, no commas,
no accents. The display title lives in `title` below, so the file on disk
never has to be pretty. This is not fussiness — both other spellings were
tried and both 404'd:
- A comma percent-encoded as %2C never resolves. Vite's static server
decodes with decodeURI, which by specification leaves the reserved
characters alone, so it went looking for a file with a literal '%2C'
in its name.
- An accented character is worse, because it fails in only one place.
macOS wrote 'Chevres' decomposed (e + U+0300) while git recorded it
precomposed (U+00E8). APFS compares normalisation-insensitively so it
resolved locally either way; Linux, which is what Netlify serves from,
compares bytes, so the deployed file and the URL in this manifest were
two different names. It worked on the laptop and 404'd in production.
Staying inside ASCII means the path needs no encoding at all and cannot
drift between the filesystem, git and the CDN.
These tracks were written and titled by the site's author under the name
cyberpantz, and generated with Suno. Both halves matter: the prompting and
selection are his, the audio came out of a model. Recorded here so the
provenance travels with the files rather than living in someone's memory.
Fetched at runtime, so adding a song is editing this file — no rebuild, and
the deck never enters the JS bundle.
Only `title` and `src` are required. `duration` is in seconds and optional;
it lets the list show a length before the file has been touched. These were
read off the files with ffprobe.
